raw_response:
I'm 57 this year, been farming these 5 mu for 30 years. My husband does construction in town part-time, and my son and daughter-in-law both work at the textile factory in Handan, so most days it's just me in the fields. The daughter-in-law helps on weekends when she's not too tired. We don't have much land, but the soil is good, and I've learned you don't get ahead by wasting money on things you don't need.

I'll plant wheat around October 10th, same as always. I'm using Jinmai 47 again — I've grown it for years, does well here, and the seed was decent last year. But I'll buy fresh seed this time because the germination looked a bit off at the edge of the field. Costs about 28 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, the extension station says 15 kg nitrogen per mu, but I've always done fine with a bit less. I'll put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's my base — and then at jointing in March I'll see how the wheat looks. If it's yellowing, I'll topdress with another 15 kg of urea per mu. So that's about 14 kg nitrogen total. The compound fertilizer gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, maybe 7–8 kg each. I don't bother buying extra phosphorus or potassium fertilizer — the soil's decent enough and I need to watch my cash.

I'll irrigate three times for the wheat: once in winter if it's too dry, once at jointing, and once at heading. Pumping costs money — each time is about 35–40 yuan for electricity — so I don't water more than I need. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see rust in the spring I'll spray fungicide. Otherwise I save that money. Last year I didn't need fungicide, but you never know.

For maize, it's always a rush after wheat harvest in early June. I hire the neighbor's tractor to rotary-till right away, then plant within two days — that window is so tight, if you miss it the yield drops. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar, about 45 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I just put 40 kg of compound fertilizer down at planting, about 10 kg nitrogen worth. No time and no money for topdressing, and anyway the maize usually does alright with that. That's about 5 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium too. I'll irrigate once or twice depending on the rain in July and August. Wet summer, maybe just once. Dry year, twice.

Labor is mostly me and my husband when he's home. For wheat harvest and maize planting, those are the busiest times — I might hire two days of help each at 120 yuan per day. The rest I do myself. Wheat takes more time with harvest and threshing and hauling. Maize is quicker except that planting rush.

I expect about 400 kg per mu of wheat and maybe 450 kg per mu of maize. Last year was decent, soil looks about the same. I'm not expecting miracles — just steady, don't lose money, have enough grain for the family and some to sell. Total costs will run about 3,500 yuan. That's a lot for us, but we need to eat.
